replies.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
replies.body:
The color pallette is basically claude default, the entire UI is just claude boxes, you could have tweaked it for years or you could have sent 1 prompt "make the UI" and both would have looked the exact same, that's why people tend to say 'no effort' and 'slop' for those looks. If you like it, that's good, but if you want other people to like it, you have to tailor it to what other people deem as good looking.

For me personally, the gameplay looks way too busy, too many colors without any hierarchy, too many VFX elements firing giving that 'epic' destruction feel/look that I can't tell what is happening, but then again, I may not be the target for this type of game/look and other would find it good.

One note, not long ago, someone posted a similar game that runs in HTML, the gameplay was practically the exact same as yours, the progression system etc are there, maybe not as deep as yours, I didn't get in depth in either of them to tell, but that was there for free as a quick couple of hours hobby project and I suspect there are a ton of those on steam and on other stores/free, I didn't see anything in your game that stands out to me or tells me that your game is any different, at least not from the trailor.  
P.S. made for x platform and ported to y platform is not a good point to advertise, people hate badly ported games and give them extra hate

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/sigistsauer please update this post with more on how you used AI to build the game. A line saying it was made with AI isn't enough. Share dev details. Rule 4 is there so promotional posts add to the sub by talking about the process and real development. We don't want the sub drowned in empty promotion. Posts that aren't updated may be removed.
